451.quote_or_event: “Kabeer, I have been ruined and destroyed by bad company, like the banana plant near the thorn bush.” … “The thorn bush waves in the wind, and pierces the banana plant; see this, and do not associate with the faithless cynics.”
451.explanation: Bhagat Kabir pictures bad company as a thorn bush that tears the tender banana plant beside it, and warns the seeker to keep away from the faithless (saakat).
451.tie_back: The Kural says greatness fears the company of the mean while smallness embraces it; Kabir shows why the wise shrink from such company and urges them to avoid it.
451.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1369, Salok Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
451._accuracy_note: A strong fit on fearing and avoiding mean company; Kabir does not draw the Kural's contrast with the small-minded who gather such people as kin.

452.quote_or_event: “Kabeer, the mind has become a bird; it soars and flies in the ten directions. According to the company it keeps, so are the fruits it eats.”
452.explanation: Bhagat Kabir compares the restless mind to a bird whose nourishment depends on where it settles, that is, on the company it keeps.
452.tie_back: The Kural says understanding takes on the nature of one's company as water takes on the nature of the soil; Kabir says the mind feeds on whatever its company offers.
452.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1369, Salok Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
452._accuracy_note: Near one-to-one on the mind being shaped by its company; the images differ (a bird eating fruit versus water taking on the soil's nature).

453.quote_or_event: “Of all plants, the sandalwood tree is the most sublime. Everything near the sandalwood tree becomes fragrant like sandalwood.”
453.explanation: Guru Ram Das uses the sandalwood tree, which perfumes everything growing near it, as an image of the saints whose company transforms those around them.
453.tie_back: The Kural says the verdict 'he is such-and-such a man' comes from one's company; Guru Ram Das likewise shows plants taking on the very name and nature of what they stand beside.
453.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 834, Raag Bilaaval, Guru Ram Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
453._accuracy_note: A strong thematic fit on being known and shaped by one's company; the Kural stresses public reputation, whereas the Guru stresses inner transformation.

454.quote_or_event: “In the Company of the Holy, spiritual wisdom is revealed.”
454.explanation: In the Sukhmani Guru Arjan teaches that true wisdom (sugiaan) comes to light within the Saadh Sangat.
454.tie_back: The Kural says wisdom only seems to live in one's own mind but really resides in one's company; Guru Arjan places the revelation of wisdom in holy company.
454.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 271, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
454._accuracy_note: A strong fit: both locate wisdom in company rather than the isolated mind; Gurbani's wisdom is spiritual knowledge of God rather than worldly judgement.

455.quote_or_event: “In the Company of the Holy, all filth is removed.”
455.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that the Saadh Sangat washes away the filth of vice from the mind.
455.tie_back: The Kural says purity of mind and of deeds comes through purity of company; Guru Arjan says holy company is what cleanses a person.
455.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 271, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
455._accuracy_note: A strong fit on company as the source of purity; the line does not separate purity of mind from purity of action as the Kural does.

456.quote_or_event: “In the Company of the Holy, one's feet do not wander.”
456.explanation: Guru Arjan says that in holy company a person does not step onto crooked paths; commentators gloss the line as not taking a step towards wrongdoing.
456.tie_back: The Kural says those whose company is pure do no deed that is not good; Guru Arjan likewise says that in pure company one's steps do not go astray.
456.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 271, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
456._accuracy_note: A strong fit on the second line of the Kural; the first line's idea of a good legacy or progeny left by the pure-minded is not covered.

457.quote_or_event: “The poor castor oil plant, growing near the sandalwood tree, becomes fragrant; in the same way, the sinner, associating with the Saints, becomes acceptable and approved.”
457.explanation: Guru Ram Das says even the lowly castor plant takes on sandalwood's fragrance, and even a sinner gains honour and acceptance through the company of the saints.
457.tie_back: The Kural says good company brings every kind of renown; Guru Ram Das shows company raising even the humblest to honour and approval.
457.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 861, Raag Gond, Guru Ram Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
457._accuracy_note: A strong fit on company conferring honour; Gurbani's 'approval' is acceptance in God's court rather than worldly fame, and the Kural's first half (prosperity from goodness of mind) is not addressed.

458.quote_or_event: “In the Company of the Holy, the mind becomes stable.”
458.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that the Saadh Sangat steadies the mind so that it stops wandering.
458.tie_back: The Kural says even the already-virtuous gain security and strength from good company; Guru Arjan presents holy company as the steadying support of the mind.
458.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 271, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
458._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: the line speaks of stability from company but not specifically of the already-wise needing it, which is the Kural's distinctive point.

459.quote_or_event: “In the Company of the Holy, one meets the Incomprehensible Lord.”
459.explanation: Guru Arjan teaches that union with God, the highest spiritual goal, is reached within the Saadh Sangat.
459.tie_back: The Kural says even bliss in the world to come is made secure by goodness of company; Guru Arjan makes holy company the place where the soul meets God.
459.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 271, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
459._accuracy_note: A strong thematic fit on company securing the highest spiritual good; Sikh teaching speaks of union with God here and now rather than a reward in the next world.

460.quote_or_event: “Kabeer, associate with the Holy people, who will take you to Nirvaanaa in the end. Do not associate with the faithless cynics; they would bring you to ruin.”
460.explanation: Bhagat Kabir sets the two kinds of company side by side: holy company stays with you to the end and brings liberation, while the company of the faithless brings destruction.
460.tie_back: The Kural ends the chapter by saying no help is greater than good company and nothing causes more affliction than bad company; Kabir gives the same two-sided verdict.
460.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1369, Salok Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
460._accuracy_note: Near one-to-one in structure and verdict; Kabir's 'good company' is specifically the company of the devout, and his stakes are spiritual liberation versus ruin.
